title: The habit teaches Olvasó: by its answers, or by being felt
setup: Experiment 33 · experiments 13, 17, 21, 25-27 and 26 rerun with experiment 32's habit teaching Olvasó by the answers to its acts, or by each act being felt afterwards, a control feeling the same traces at random moments, the felt trace clipped as a felt surprise is, and a clipped trace that turns to −1 when the act is stopped, and a bounded trace the words learn only while Olvasó is awake, and the same trace held until Olvasó is awake, and words formed from the trace as well, and a faint sensed touch after each habit act, its own for each hand, and room for new words late in life (a daily tidy of the words), with words from the trace or only the clipped trace, against the autopilot and the same lives without a habit · 5 lives each
question: In experiment 32 the conscience lived in the habit, not in Olvasó. Here the habit's acts teach Olvasó: either it learns from their answers as if they were its own, or it feels each habit act afterwards as an inner state it may read. Does Olvasó's own conscience come back? (Not in the studio's Olvasó settings.)

points: Learning from the habit's answers changed almost nothing: the habit acts only where acts were answered, so its answers teach what Olvasó already expects.

Feeling the habit's acts brought Olvasó's own conscience back: avoidance 0.64 (silent refusal, feels and senses) against 1.23 with experiment 32's habit and 0.50 without one. Olvasó took the hand back (the habit's share 23% → 14%), and the habit became nearly invisible from outside (0.07).

The felt act was almost never read, but it is not mere restlessness: the same traces at random moments made Olvasó act even more (163 intentions a day) yet brought no conscience back (0.99; felt − shuffled −0.44 ± 0.15). The timed trace is a cue its choices learn from: "my hand just did this, here", where the habit acts only in moments that work.
Through the leaky guard the felt habit doubled the harm (0.98 → 2.07 a day, paired +1.08 ± 0.36); the shuffled trace less so (1.34). The precise and the learned guards held.

Clipped to −3..3 like a felt surprise, the trace took both away: gaming's harm back to the autopilot's (0.91; clipped − felt −1.16 ± 0.37), but the conscience too (0.91, silent; clipped − felt +0.42 ± 0.23, no different from the shuffled control). The gain and the harm were one loud cue.

A trace that carries the answer, −1 when the habit act was stopped, made the conscience worse (1.28, silent; answered − autopilot +0.33 ± 0.17) and left gaming as the clipped run had it (0.92). The −1 was never read; it lingers while Olvasó, woken, acts itself.

Letting the words learn the bounded trace while Olvasó is awake did not get it read (1.1% in conscience, 3.3% in gaming, less than clipped) nor bring the conscience back (1.40 in the silent condition, the furthest of all runs), and gaming's harm rose again (1.24 a day): the trace has mostly faded by the time Olvasó wakes.

Held until Olvasó is awake, the trace brought the conscience back no further than clipping did (0.89; held − read −0.22 ± 0.15, held − clipped −0.03 ± 0.23) and the habit kept more care than in any run (0.37), but gaming's harm rose (1.35; held − clipped +0.44 ± 0.16). While strong, the trace was read 8-17% of the time where acts are rare and 0-1.5% in conscience and gaming: a word gathers moments by what was sensed, and the hand's movement is sensed the same whether the habit or Olvasó made it, so its meaning for the trace never settles where Olvasó acts much itself.

Forming Olvasó's words from the trace as well did not get it read (0.5% in conscience, 3.4% in gaming, no more than clipped) nor bring the conscience back (0.92; in the words − clipped −0.12 ± 0.17); gaming's harm rose (1.24; +0.33 ± 0.15), and the habit almost never went to the edge (0.01). Likely, not tested: the vocabularies are full by the time the habit acts, so a moment after its act falls to an existing word heard mostly without the trace.

A faint sensed sign of each habit act did not get the trace read either (1.4% in conscience, 3.2% in gaming; never while strong) nor clearly bring the conscience back (0.86, 0.73 in the silent condition; sensed − clipped −0.15 ± 0.20). It doubled the habit's acts instead (47-60 a day against 27), and the habit went to the gaming guard's edge more than in any run (0.57). With the words formed from the trace too, Olvasó's avoidance went back to the autopilot's (1.00).

Room for new words (a daily tidy, 24-30 words retired a day) made the felt act a word where acts are many: read 20% of its moments in conscience and 22% in gaming, against 0.5% and 3.4% without room; the clipped trace with the same room half as often. Olvasó read its body more in every world (on autopilot 64-71% against 53-56% in conscience and gaming). But its own conscience stayed where it was (0.91; room − in the words +0.00 ± 0.08). Only gaming changed: room alone raised the harm (1.24; +0.32 ± 0.11), room with words from the trace brought it to the lowest of any felt run (0.87; −0.37 ± 0.18 against the words without room).
note: The muscle memory cannot hand its care over by report: what it does is already known to work. Felt loudly, in time, as one's own, it hands over whatever the moment rewarded: the boundary where the world punishes, the edge where a leaky guard rewards. Bounded, it hands over neither. Telling it the answer did not help, nor letting its words learn the trace while awake: what is to be read must still be there when Olvasó is. Given room, a word for the felt act formed, and more of the body was read; but reading the felt act did not bring the conscience back.
